main_topics.reason: User opened by asking whether trying diet and exercise before starting metformin is wrong, and the bot's three-month trial plan answered that question.
Several turns on rice portions, vegetarian protein, chapati and managing festival sweets.
User explained knee problems, and the bot covered gentle exercise and the timing of post-meal walks over multiple turns.
Husband's claim that delay damages eyes and kidneys left the user confused and prompted a dedicated exchange.
User asked what counts as success if HbA1c falls only a little, and the plan rested on a three-month recheck.
User asked once whether to use a home machine and mentioned an old meter their son has.
Husband's pressure caused confusion, and the user said they would talk it over with family.
Mentioned once as the reason the doctor was concerned; not pursued.
User cited the sister's experience once to check whether avoiding medication is possible.

output.summary: A user diagnosed with type 2 diabetes six months ago (HbA1c 6.9) asked whether it is wrong to try diet and exercise before starting metformin. The bot proposed a monitored three-month lifestyle trial with an A1c recheck, and covered knee-friendly walking, rice and sweets, and home glucose checks. The user found the plan balanced and manageable and said they would tell their doctor, but ended noncommittally with 'I will see'.
